description:
Make the user-facing docs/metadata reflect the Gemini backend before publishing v1.1.0. This session's audit found the README is 100% Codex with one active inaccuracy and one stale error code.

README.md changes:
- Title/intro/pitch → provider-neutral (Codex default, Gemini as an option; "$0 with your ChatGPT (Codex) or Google AI Pro (Gemini) subscription").
- Add a Gemini Quick Start: install the Antigravity `agy` CLI, run `agy` once to sign in (Google AI Pro), set `"provider": "gemini"`.
- Document the `provider` config field; add the Gemini recommended-models table (Gemini 3.5 Flash (Medium/High), Gemini 3.1 Pro (High)) + `"latest"`; note reasoning_effort is baked into the agy model name (ignored for Gemini, emits a startup note).
- Provider-neutral architecture diagram (codex SDK + agy CLI behind the backend seam).
- FIX inaccuracy: the `model` tool-param tables say "Incompatible with session_id" — now Codex-only; Gemini ALLOWS model override on a resumed session (M1).
- FIX stale error code: troubleshooting references `CODEX_TIMEOUT`, renamed to `REVIEW_TIMEOUT`. Add Gemini/agy rows: CONFIG_ERROR (agy not found), AUTH_ERROR (agy not signed in), PROVIDER_MISMATCH.

package.json: description hardcodes "OpenAI Codex" → provider-neutral; keywords add "gemini".

OPEN QUESTION: repo documents agy sign-in ("run `agy` once") but NOT an install command — confirm the canonical agy install reference before writing that section; do not fabricate.

Note: docs/ is gitignored; the live probe checklist lives in docs/hardening-probes.md (local only). Blocks the v1.1.0 publish ticket.
title: Update README + package.json for multi-provider
